questions.q: A screenwriter wants a confession scene to feel dangerous and secretive. Which lighting should the scene description suggest?
choices: Low-key lighting, with one strong source and deep shadows
Flat lighting so nothing distracts from the dialogue
questions.explain: Low-key lighting, with strong contrast and deep shadow, reads as hidden and dangerous; high-key reads as open and safe.

questions.q: In a mostly black-and-white film, one small girl wears a red coat, and the coat is glimpsed again later. What is this?
questions.explain: A colour motif gives one colour a meaning that builds each time it returns, as in Schindler's List.

questions.q: Which four things do Bordwell and Thompson group under mise-en-scène?
choices: Setting, costume and makeup, lighting, and staging
Shot size, angle, movement and focus
Dialogue, music, sound effects and silence
questions.explain: Mise-en-scène is what's placed in front of the camera; camera and editing are separate categories.

questions.q: A novelist writes that the sky 'wept' at a funeral. What did John Ruskin, who coined the term for this, think of it?
choices: He praised it as the mark of the greatest poets
He thought it belonged only to comedy
He called it a 'fallacy': strong feeling producing a false picture of nature
questions.explain: Ruskin's 'pathetic fallacy' (1856) was critical in intent; the neutral modern use came later.

questions.q: In Parasite, the rich family live on a hill and the poor family in a semi-basement, and a storm floods only the lower home. Which tool is carrying the film's argument most directly?
choices: Production design: setting that embodies the conflict
questions.explain: The geography of the sets, up and down, makes class visible.

questions.q: A young boy plays in the snow, seen through a distant window, while in the foreground his mother signs him away. What is the shot using?
choices: Blocking in depth within the frame
questions.explain: Placing characters near and far in one frame tells the story: the boy's future is decided out of his hearing.

questions.q: A critic insists every red object in a film is a hidden symbol to be decoded. Which thinker in this course would push back?
questions.explain: Sontag warned against translating works into hidden meanings instead of attending to form and sensation.

ideas: Everything placed in front of the camera, from the setting to the light to the actors' positions, tells the audience how to feel before anyone speaks.
A director's personal style shows less in the script than in how each scene is staged, lit and arranged.
A single colour, repeated and then paid off, can work as a setup and payoff made of light.
Weather that mirrors a character's feelings began as a criticism: emotion giving a false picture of nature.
